analyst_view.overall: Slavia are 34th of 36 with 1 point and Villarreal 28th with 3, so both are below the top-24 line and need a win; Slavia, still looking for a first Champions League win under Jindrich Trpisovsky, lead the Czech league after winning 2-0 at Olomouc, while Villarreal lost 3-2 at Barcelona on Sunday after leading 2-0. Slavia are without Stepan Chaloupek, David Moses, Elias Pitak and Danijel Sturm as well as the counted Adonija Ouanda, and Lukas Provod (illness after international duty) still needs a late check; only Ouanda and Ogbu are in the numbers. Villarreal are still without Gerard Moreno, Juan Foyth and Ilias Akhomach, who are back near group training but listed out for this game and not counted by the numbers, plus the counted Alassane Diatta, and one report says midfielder Nathan Saliba has ankle discomfort awaiting tests. Absences on both sides roughly cancel out, so the view stays with the numbers; Slovenian referee Rade Obrenovic, with a slightly low card record, is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals (1.2 Slavia, 2.4 Villarreal), already counting both sides' recent scoring and Diatta's absence. Villarreal still lack Gerard Moreno and Akhomach up front, while Slavia lose Moses and maybe Provod from midfield; both teams need a win, so these pull both ways and I stay at 3.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, already raised for Slavia's recent corner count (+5.7%). Slavia attack down the flanks with wing-backs Vlcek and Jurasek and Villarreal play wide through Buchanan and Moleiro; that is the game the numbers expect, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards, already taking off Slavia's unusually low recent card count (-9.0%) and Rade Obrenovic's slightly low record (-2.1%), and adding a little for Villarreal's (+1.8%). Two teams that both need the result can make for a tense game, and Mourino is one booking from a ban, but there is no bad blood, so I stay at 4.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.2 shots, already lifted for both sides' heavy recent shooting (+15.9% Slavia, +8.2% Villarreal). Slavia's high-tempo home game fits that picture; Villarreal's missing attackers and a possible absence for Saliba could cut a little, but they still scored twice at Barcelona, so I stay at 31.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target, already counting Slavia's sharper recent finishing (+11.2%). With uncounted absences on both sides (Moses and maybe Provod for Slavia, Gerard Moreno and Akhomach for Villarreal) nothing tips it, so I stay at 10.1.
